title: Diversity-Aware Ensemble of Quantum-Classical Models via Combinatorial Fusion
authors: Jingyan Xu, Yuanhong Wu, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Sean Patten, Christina Schweikert, D. Frank Hsu
abstract: Variational quantum circuits (VQCs) are highly sensitive to circuit architecture, yet most quantum machine learning pipelines select a single best design and discard the remaining candidates. This paper addresses whether the structural diversity across quantum circuit search spaces can be used to produce stronger predictions through model fusion. We apply Combinatorial Fusion Analysis (CFA), a model fusion framework that selects and combines multiple scoring systems using rank-score function (RSF) and cognitive diversity (CD), to a pool of 29 architecturally diverse classical models and quantum circuits. Using a diversity-aware model selection method, we identify subsets of maximally diverse models and combine them with both score and rank combination. Experiments on four binary classification benchmarks covering different domains demonstrate that CFA-based hybrid classical-quantum fusion consistently outperform the best individual model on every dataset considered with improvements up to 6.03% in accuracy. When comparing with relevant literatures, the CFA framework further achieves superior performance across all four datasets.
summary: This work proposes Combinatorial Fusion Analysis (CFA) to improve Quantum Machine Learning by fusing predictions from multiple, architecturally diverse quantum circuits. CFA uses cognitive diversity and rank-score functions to systematically combine model outputs. The method proves superior to single-model approaches across various classification tasks, highlighting the value of structural diversity in quantum model ensembles.
main_problem: The paper addresses the limitation of current Quantum Machine Learning (QML) pipelines that select only a single best quantum circuit architecture, ignoring structural diversity.
main_result: A novel framework, Combinatorial Fusion Analysis (CFA), combining predictions from diverse quantum and classical models consistently outperforms the best individual model on multiple binary classification benchmarks, showing improvements up to 6.03%.
method: CFA is a model fusion framework that combines multiple scoring systems using the Rank-Score Function (RSF) and quantifies model dissimilarity via Cognitive Diversity (CD).
model_or_system: The models are Variational Quantum Circuits (VQCs) acting as trainable function approximators within hybrid quantum-classical machine learning pipelines. The search space involves architecturally diverse circuits.
important_parameters: The search space is defined by choices like Hadamard Initialization, Encoding Rotation, and Entangling Topology.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that structural diversity across quantum circuit architectures can be leveraged to enhance predictive power through model fusion.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the general VQC architecture flow, and Figure 2 shows three representative circuit architectures on 4 qubits.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of single-model reliance in QML, proposes the CFA framework using RSF and CD to measure diversity, and validates this fusion approach on four distinct binary classification benchmarks.
why_interesting: While focused on ML, the rigorous quantification of structural diversity (CD) and the systematic combination of multiple quantum models provides a novel, data-driven approach to characterizing the robustness and potential of complex quantum circuits.
